Built-in Formula Library (FMLA)

Twenty-three factory algorithms in ROM. Press FMLA, enter 01–23, then supply prompted parameters.

keys
FMLA

Built-in formulas live in ROM and do not use the 680-byte program pool. HKEAA SUPER-FX PLUS sittings still allow student programs in P1–P4; FMLA is a verified factory routine, not a substitute for writing your own solver.

steps

General procedure

  1. Press FMLA
  2. Enter two-digit index (01–23)
  3. Enter each prompted variable, confirming with EXE
  4. Read the computed result

Formula catalog

  • [FMLA 01] QuadEquationSolve ax² + bx + c = 0 for real roots. Two distinct roots, one repeated root, or MATH ERROR when there are no real roots.
  • [FMLA 02] CosineTheoremFind a side opposite angle A in a triangle (law of cosines).
  • [FMLA 03] HeronFormulaTriangle area from three side lengths.
  • [FMLA 04] NormalPStandard normal CDF up to x (Hastings approximation). Prompt is x; range 0 ≤ x < 10⁵⁰.
  • [FMLA 05] NormalQStandard normal probability from 0 to x (Casio Q; Hastings approximation). Prompt is x; range 0 ≤ x < 10⁵⁰.
  • [FMLA 06] CoulombLawElectrostatic force between two point charges.
  • [FMLA 07] ResistanceOhmic resistance from resistivity, length, and cross-section.
  • [FMLA 08] MagneticForceForce on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
  • [FMLA 09] RCVoltageResistor terminal voltage VR in an RC series circuit after a DC voltage V is applied (exponential decay).
  • [FMLA 10] VoltageGainDecibel voltage gain between input and output.
  • [FMLA 11] SeriesLRCSeries RLC impedance at frequency f. Type f in Hz; the ROM uses 2πf, not a separate ω prompt.
  • [FMLA 12] ParallelLRCParallel RLC impedance at frequency f. Type f in Hz; the ROM uses 2πf, not a separate ω prompt.
  • [FMLA 13] OscillationLC tank resonant frequency.
  • [FMLA 14] DropDistanceVertical displacement under constant g from ROM (CONST 9-3 = 9.80665).
  • [FMLA 15] SimpPendulumPeriod of a simple pendulum for small angles.
  • [FMLA 16] SprgPendulumPeriod of a mass-spring oscillator.
  • [FMLA 17] DopplerObserved frequency when source and observer move. The ROM uses one signed formula, not the textbook ± form.
  • [FMLA 18] IdealGasState equation; uses gas constant R from ROM.
  • [FMLA 19] CentrifugalCentripetal/centrifugal magnitude for circular motion.
  • [FMLA 20] ElasticEnergyPotential energy stored in a stretched/compressed spring.
  • [FMLA 21] BernoulliIncompressible steady flow. The calculator prints C = v²/2 + gz + P/ρ (energy per unit mass), not the pressure-form constant.
  • [FMLA 22] StadiaHeightSurveying stadia elevation difference from staff interval s and elevation angle θ (Deg), with instrument constants K and C.
  • [FMLA 23] StadiaDistSurveying stadia horizontal distance.
